articles.summary: OpsPilot is one platform, not 25 chatbots. Every agent is a thin, typed module that plugs into shared infrastructure: the orchestrator, tool registry, policy engine, approval service, LLM gateway,…
articles.body:
OpsPilot is one platform, not 25 chatbots. Every agent is a thin, typed module that plugs into shared infrastructure: the orchestrator, tool registry, policy engine, approval service, LLM gateway, durable state and audit log. ## System diagram ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Clients UI[Next.js dashboard
same-origin /api/v1 proxy] WH[Provider webhooks
signed] API_C[API clients
X-API-Key] MCPC[MCP clients
Claude Desktop / Code] end subgraph API["FastAPI (api/v1)"] AUTH[Auth: OIDC JWT / local JWT / API keys
tenant from credential only] EV[/events/] WF[/workflows/] AG[/agents/] AP[/approvals/] ADM[/admin, integrations, reports, audit/] COP[/copilot, tools, custom-tools, batches, system/] MCP[/mcp Streamable HTTP/] end subgraph Core["Shared platform"] ORCH[Workflow orchestrator
graph runner · checkpoints · resume · parallel · bounded delegation] RUN[Agent runner
validate in/out · budgets · usage] REG[(Agent registry
25 specs)] POL[Policy engine
allow / approve / deny] ACT[Action service
idempotency · verify · dead-letter] APR[Approval service
payload-hash bound · SoD · expiry] TOOLS[(Tool registry
98 typed tools)] LLM[LLM gateway
mock / Anthropic / OpenAI
structured output · safety] RAG[Retrieval
BM25 (+pgvector)] LOOP[Ops Copilot tool loop
Claude tool use / offline planner
agents + read tools + custom tools as tools] CUST[Custom HTTP tools
SSRF guard · encrypted secret] end subgraph Integrations RES[Adapter resolver] MOCK[13 sandbox adapters
tenant sandbox records] LIVE[7 live adapters
Slack · HubSpot · SendGrid · Jira · Shopify · WhatsApp · Zendesk] end subgraph Data["PostgreSQL (RLS) / SQLite dev"] DB[(28 tables: tenants, users, roles, integrations,
agent defs/versions, workflow defs/runs/checkpoints,
agent runs, approvals, tool executions, tasks,
documents/chunks, audit (hash chain), metrics, usage,
incidents, dead letters, idempotency, sandbox records)] end subgraph Workers Q[Durable DB job queue
leases · retries · dead jobs · dedupe · tenant caps] WK[Worker processes ×N
app.workers.runner / in-process pool / Celery] BEAT[Maintenance: expire approvals · reap leases · recover stale runs ·
reconcile unknown executions · seal audit chain · metrics · retention] end UI --> API WH --> EV API_C --> EV MCPC --> MCP --> RUN MCP --> ORCH COP --> Q Q --> WK --> LOOP WK --> ORCH LOOP -->|agent__*| RUN LOOP -->|read tools| TOOLS LOOP -->|custom__*| POL ACT --> CUST EV --> ORCH WF --> ORCH AG --> RUN AP --> APR ORCH --> Q ORCH --> RUN --> REG RUN --> LLM RUN --> RAG RUN -->|read-only tools| TOOLS RUN -->|proposed actions| POL --> ACT POL -->|require approval| APR --> ACT ACT --> TOOLS --> RES RES --> MOCK RES --> LIVE Core --> DB BEAT --> DB ``` ## Request lifecycle (the 15 orchestrator steps) 1. **Receive** — `POST /events` (user/API-key auth) or `POST /webhooks/{tenant}/{provider}` (HMAC-verified). 2. **Authenticate & resolve tenant** — only from the verified JWT/API key/webhook secret, never from the body. 3. **Validate & deduplicate** — payload size limits; `(tenant, dedupe_key)` unique constraint; duplicates return the original event and run. 4. **Select workflow** — `EVENT_ROUTING` (event type → workflow key) or explicit `workflow_key`; tenant-specific definitions override platform templates. 5. **Retrieve context** — agents read only through allowed, read-only tools (CRM, orders, knowledge base…). 6. **Dispatch agent** — `run_agent` validates input against the agent's Pydantic model, builds `AgentContext`, enforces token budget and tool-call limits. 7. **Validate result** — output validated against the declared output model; evidence refs checked; unsupported links/figures stripped by the agents themselves. 8. **Policy** — `evaluate_action` decides allow / require_approval / deny per proposed action, deterministically. 9. **Approval** — `Approval` row bound to `sha256(tool, type, payload, tenant, agent)`; run status → `waiting_approval`. 10. **Execute** — `ActionService.execute` writes an `in_progress` `ToolExecution` **before** calling the provider (crash marker), uses idempotency keys, and never resends a non-idempotent action after a timeout. 11. **Verify** — unknown outcomes are reconciled via `adapter.verify_action` (now or by the maintenance job). 12. **Persist** — each node transition is a `WorkflowCheckpoint`; the run's `state.nodes` holds every agent's structured output. 13. **Retry** — transient errors re-enqueue the run with backoff (bounded by `MAX_RUN_ATTEMPTS`); terminal failures open an `Incident` and a `DeadLetter`. 14. **Resume** — `recover_stale_runs` re-enqueues runs whose worker heartbeat stopped; execution continues from `current_node`. 15. **Return** — `GET /workflows/{id}` returns status, checkpoints, agent runs, pending approvals, graph and correlation id. ## Agent contract ```python class AgentSpec: key, name, department, version, description, use_cases, input_model, output_model, allowed_tools, permission_scopes, policies, approval_rules, timeout_seconds, token_budget, risk_level, model_tier, evaluation_dataset, baseline_minutes_saved class AgentContext: tenant_id, actor_id, workflow_run_id, agent_run_id, correlation_id, permissions, policy_version, node_key, depth, tenant_config, agent_config, now class AgentResult: status, data, evidence_refs, evidence, missing_information, proposed_actions, warnings, summary, confidence, estimated_minutes_saved ``` Agents receive `AgentServices` with a **scoped `ToolInvoker`** (allowlist + permission + read-only + call limit enforcement, every call recorded as a `ToolExecution`) and the LLM gateway. They return `ProposedAction`s; they cannot execute side effects. ### Deterministic vs model work | Deterministic code | Model (with heuristic fallback) | |---|---| | routing, permissions, policy, approvals, idempotency | extraction from free text (transcripts, invoices, bug reports) | | all money math (Decimal), scores, forecasts, KPIs, SLAs, deadlines | summaries and narratives (checked for unsupported figures/causal claims) | | duplicate detection, 3-way matching, evidence validation | classification (intent, category) — then re-validated against rules | Every model call goes through `LLMGateway.structured()` with a Pydantic schema and a `heuristic` callable. Under `LLM_PROVIDER=mock` the heuristic *is* the implementation, which is why the whole platform works offline and why tests are deterministic. With a real provider, the heuristic is only used as a labelled fallback after retries (`model="heuristic-fallback"` + warning), never silently. ## Workflow graphs Workflows are JSON graphs of typed nodes (`agent`, `condition`, `approval_gate`, `parallel`, `workflow`, `action`, `end`) with `$.input…` / `$.nodes..data…` input mapping. Ten built-in templates live in `orchestration/definitions.py`; tenants can add their own via `POST /workflows/definitions` (validated: known node types, known agents, existing targets). Bounds: `WORKFLOW_MAX_STEPS`, `MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH = 3`, per-run deadline, per-agent token budget and `MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_RUN`. ## Multi-tenancy * Every tenant-owned table has a non-null `tenant_id` (+ index); all queries filter on the authenticated principal's tenant. * On PostgreSQL the hardening migration enables **row-level security** with a policy on `current_setting('app.current_tenant')`, which `set_tenant_context` sets per session. Run the API/workers as the `opspilot_app` role so RLS applies. * Sandbox data (`business_records`) is tenant-scoped too, so demo data never crosses tenants. * Quotas (`workflow runs`, `LLM tokens` per month) are enforced at run start; per-tenant rate limits on ingestion and agent runs. ## What is mock vs live | Component | Mock / sandbox | Live | |---|---|---| | LLM | `MockProvider` + per-agent heuristics (default) | Anthropic / OpenAI via official SDKs when keys are set (the Anthropic path is unit-tested against a fake client only; no live call was made in this repository) | | Ops Copilot | deterministic offline planner drives the same tool loop | Claude tool use (`claude-opus-5-5`) when `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` | | Custom tools | — | always real HTTPS calls to the tenant's endpoint (tests use `httpx.MockTransport`) | | CRM, email, chat, issues, helpdesk, commerce, accounting, WhatsApp, workspace, monitoring, procurement, feedback, metrics | 13 sandbox adapters over tenant sandbox records (persistent, idempotent, verifiable) | HubSpot, SendGrid, Slack, Jira, Shopify, WhatsApp Cloud API, Zendesk (documented REST APIs, `httpx`, tested with `MockTransport` only — **not** validated against real accounts in this repo) | | Accounting, procurement, workspace (Google), monitoring (Datadog/Grafana), feedback, metrics | sandbox only | not implemented; `IntegrationNotConfigured` is raised explicitly | | Document extraction | plain text/markdown/CSV/JSON; minimal PDF literal-text extraction | plug a document-AI provider into `services/documents.extract_text` | | Embeddings / pgvector | lexical BM25 retrieval (always on) | `VectorType` column + `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`; embedding calls not wired to a provider yet | The dashboard labels every integration **Sandbox** or **Live**, and tool executions record the `mode` they ran in, so audit trails never confuse the two. ## Key design decisions * **Agents propose, the platform disposes.** No agent holds credentials or can call a side-effecting tool; the policy engine and approval service sit between every proposal and execution, and the model cannot influence their decision beyond the content it proposes. * **Crash-safe side effects.** `ToolExecution(in_progress)` is committed before the provider call; idempotency keys are derived from the payload when the agent does not supply one; unknown outcomes are verified, not retried, for non-idempotent tools. * **Approvals are bound to bytes.** The approval stores the exact payload and its hash; a mismatch (tampering or a changed action) supersedes the approval and requires a new one. Requester ≠ reviewer, expiry, and reviewer permission are enforced in code. * **Durable graph execution.** Node-level checkpoints + heartbeat make worker restarts safe in both thread and Celery modes; completed nodes are never re-run, and side effects inside a re-run node are deduplicated by idempotency key. * **Portable storage.** Custom `GUID`/`JSONType`/`VectorType` columns run on SQLite (dev/test) and PostgreSQL (prod) from the same models and migrations; the full test suite runs on both. * **The queue is a table.** Jobs live in PostgreSQL next to the state they act on, so enqueueing is transactional with the change that caused it, and scaling out is "start another worker process". Workers claim with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, hold renewable leases, and retry with backoff; per-tenant concurrency caps keep tenants fair. Celery remains an option, not a requirement. * **Model-driven tool use without giving the model authority.** The Copilot lets Claude choose which agents and tools to call and in what order, but every tool it can see is filtered by the user's RBAC, built-in tools exposed to it are read-only, agents it calls still only propose, and custom side-effecting tools go through the same policy engine and hash-bound approvals. * **Audit writes don't contend.** Events carry a content hash; a per-tenant sealer links committed events into the chain. Concurrent workers therefore never fork the chain or serialise on it. * **Estimated ≠ realized.** ROI reporting keeps estimated labour value and finance-verified realized savings separate, with a default realization rate of 0.

articles.body:
Base URL: `http://<host>:8000/api/v1`. Interactive docs: `/docs` (Swagger) and `/redoc`; the
OpenAPI document is at `/openapi.json`. All responses are JSON.

## Authentication

| Method | Header | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Bearer JWT (local issuer) | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from `POST /auth/login` | dashboard users (dev; disable with `ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN=false`) |
| Bearer JWT (OIDC) | token issued by your IdP; verified against `OIDC_JWKS_URL` | SSO users, mapped by `sub` to `users.external_subject` |
| API key | `X-API-Key: opk_…` created in Admin → API keys | machine clients (event ingestion, reporting) |
| Webhook signature | `X-OpsPilot-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hmac-sha256>`; Meta `X-Hub-Signature-256`; Shopify `X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256` | provider webhooks (no bearer token) |

The tenant is always derived from the verified credential. Tenant IDs in request bodies are ignored.

**Permissions** are strings like `workflows:write`; roles aggregate them (`admin` = `*`;
`platform:admin` must be granted explicitly). Every endpoint lists its required permission in
the OpenAPI description. Approvals must be decided by human users (API keys are refused).

## Conventions

* **Pagination**: `limit` (max 200/500) and `offset`; responses are `{items, total, limit, offset}`.
* **Filtering**: documented query parameters per endpoint (e.g. `status`, `workflow_key`, `q`, `severity`, `correlation_id`).
* **Errors**: `{"error": {"code", "message", "details", "correlation_id"}}` with stable codes:
  `validation_failed` 422 · `unauthenticated` 401 · `forbidden` / `tool_not_allowed` / `tenant_isolation_violation` 403 ·
  `not_found` 404 · `conflict` 409 · `agent_disabled` 423 · `integration_not_configured` 424 · `quota_exceeded` / `rate_limited` 429 ·
  `integration_error` / `llm_error` 502 · `internal_error` 500 (never includes stack traces).
* **Correlation**: send `X-Correlation-ID` (alphanumeric, ≤ 64) or receive a generated one; it is stamped on runs, audit events and logs.
* **Idempotency**: `Idempotency-Key` header on `POST /workflows`, `POST /events`, `POST /agents/{id}/run`. A reused key with a different body returns 409. Events are additionally deduplicated by `(source, event_type, external_id)`.
* **Sensitive data**: outputs are redacted (secrets always; long free-text fields truncated unless the user holds `data:sensitive`). Credentials are write-only.

## Endpoints

### Auth
| Method & path | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/login` | — | `{tenant, email, password}` → `{access_token, expires_in, user, tenant}`; rate-limited per IP |
| `GET /auth/me` | any | current user, roles, permissions, tenant |
| `GET /auth/demo-accounts` | — | seeded demo users (empty in production) |

### Events & webhooks
| `POST /events` | `events:write` | `{source, event_type, external_id?, payload, workflow_key?}` → 202 `EventOut` (`status`: dispatched / unrouted / failed; `duplicate` flag) |
| `GET /events` | `events:read` | filters `status`, `event_type` |
| `POST /webhooks/{tenant_slug}/{provider}` | signature | normalises provider payloads (WhatsApp Cloud API, Shopify) into events |
| `GET /webhooks/{tenant_slug}/whatsapp` | — | Meta verification handshake (`hub.verify_token` from the integration config) |

### Workflows
| `POST /workflows` | `workflows:write` | `{workflow_key, input}` → 202 run (status `pending` → executes async; `inline` mode executes synchronously) |
| `GET /workflows` | `workflows:read` | `status` (comma list), `workflow_key`, `q` (run id / correlation id) |
| `GET /workflows/{run_id}` | `workflows:read` | detailed: `checkpoints[]`, `agent_runs[]`, `state.nodes`, `pending_approvals[]`, `graph`, `output` |
| `POST /workflows/{run_id}/cancel` | `workflows:write` | cancels pending/waiting runs immediately; running runs stop at the next node |
| `POST /workflows/{run_id}/retry` | `workflows:write` | failed/timed-out runs resume from the last checkpoint |
| `GET /workflows/definitions` | `workflows:read` | platform templates + tenant definitions |
| `POST /workflows/definitions` | `workflows:admin` | validated graph; versions automatically |

### Agents
| `GET /agents` | `agents:read` | all 25 with tenant enablement, config and run stats; filters `department`, `q` |
| `GET /agents/{agent_id}` | `agents:read` | contract (schemas), tools, policies, recent runs, latest evaluation |
| `PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` | `agents:admin` | `{enabled, config, model_override, disabled_reason}` |
| `POST /agents/{agent_id}/run` | `agents:run` | `{input, mode: "workflow" (durable, approval-gated) | "direct"}` → result, actions, usage, tool modes |
| `GET /agents/{agent_id}/runs` | `agents:read` | paginated run history |

### Tasks, approvals, integrations
| `GET/POST /tasks`, `PATCH /tasks/{id}` | `tasks:read` / `tasks:write` | board; `overdue=true` filter |
| `GET /approvals` | `approvals:read` | `status` (default `pending`; `all`), `risk_level`, `agent_key`, `run_id` |
| `GET /approvals/{id}` | `approvals:read` | exact payload, hash, policy, evidence, context |
| `POST /approvals/{id}/decision` | `approvals:decide` + the approval's `required_permission` | `{decision: approve|reject, note?, payload_hash?}`; executes exactly once on approve; resumes the run |
| `GET /integrations` | `integrations:read` | one row per provider family with `mode` (mock/live), status, last test |
| `GET /integrations/catalog` | `integrations:read` | families, supported live providers, required credentials |
| `POST /integrations` | `integrations:admin` | upsert; credentials encrypted at rest; live rows start `pending_test` |
| `POST /integrations/{id}/test` | `integrations:admin` | real connection test; only a passing test sets `connected` |
| `POST /integrations/{id}/sync` | `integrations:admin` | records a sync checkpoint |

### Reports, usage, audit, incidents, documents, evaluations, admin
| `GET /reports/overview?days=` | `reports:read` | dashboard overview |
| `GET /reports?days=` | `reports:read` | KPIs, ROI, per-agent and per-workflow performance |
| `GET /usage?period=YYYY-MM` | `usage:read` | metering + quotas + utilisation |
| `GET /audit-events` · `GET /audit-events/verify` | `audit:read` | searchable trail; hash-chain verification |
| `GET /incidents` · `POST /incidents/{id}/resolve` | `reports:read` / `incidents:write` | |
| `GET /documents` · `POST /documents/text` · `POST /documents/upload` · `GET /documents/search?q=` · `DELETE /documents/{id}` | `documents:*` | scanned (active PDF content, injection, secrets), chunked, indexed |
| `GET /evaluations` · `POST /evaluations/run` · `POST /evaluations/run-all` | `agents:read` / `agents:admin` | synthetic evaluation harness |
| `GET/PATCH /admin/tenant` | `tenant:read` / `tenant:admin` | settings (`policies`, `roi`), retention, **emergency_disabled**; plan/quotas need `platform:admin` |
| `GET/POST /admin/users`, `PATCH /admin/users/{id}` | `users:*` | privilege-escalation guarded |
| `GET/POST /admin/roles`, `GET /admin/permissions` | `roles:*` | |
| `GET/POST/DELETE /admin/api-keys` | `apikeys:admin` | plaintext returned once |
| `GET/POST /admin/tenants` | `platform:admin` | tenant onboarding |

### Ops Copilot (model-driven tool use)
| Method & path | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /copilot/status` | `agents:run` | mode (`claude` / `offline`), model, and the tools this user can reach |
| `POST /copilot/sessions` | `agents:run` (users only; API keys → 403) | `{message}` → 202 session; the turn runs on the job queue |
| `GET /copilot/sessions` · `GET /copilot/sessions/{id}` | `agents:run` | own sessions only (others → 403); poll the session while a message is `running`: `messages[].steps[]` are the live tool calls (`tool`, `input`, `status` ok / error / needs_approval, `output`) |
| `POST /copilot/sessions/{id}/messages` | `agents:run` | follow-up; 409 while the previous turn is still running |
| `DELETE /copilot/sessions/{id}` | `agents:run` | |

### Tools, custom tools, bulk runs, queue
| Method & path | Permission | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /tools` | `agents:read` | every built-in tool (family, risk, side effect, input schema) + this tenant's custom tools |
| `GET /custom-tools` | `integrations:read` | secrets never returned (`has_secret` only) |
| `POST /custom-tools` · `PATCH/DELETE /custom-tools/{id}` | `integrations:admin` | `{name, description, method, url_template, input_schema, headers?, auth_header_name?, auth_secret?, side_effect, risk_level, timeout_seconds}`; URL must be https and resolve to public addresses |
| `POST /custom-tools/{id}/test` | `integrations:admin` | one real call with `{input}` → `{ok, latency_ms, result, error}`; side-effecting tools also need `confirm_side_effect: true`; audited |
| `POST /agents/{agent_id}/batches` | `agents:run` | `{items: [input, …] (≤ 5,000), name?, execute_actions}` → 202; each item is validated against the agent's input schema before anything is queued |
| `GET /batches` · `GET /batches/{id}` | `agents:read` | progress counters + item results (`status` filter, paginated) |
| `POST /batches/{id}/cancel` | `agents:run` | queued items become `cancelled`; running ones finish |
| `GET /system/queue` | `reports:read` | queue depth by kind/status, live workers (heartbeats), recent and dead jobs |
| `POST /system/jobs/{id}/retry` | `tenant:admin` | re-queue a `dead` job of this tenant |

### MCP (Model Context Protocol)
`POST /mcp` (Streamable HTTP, stateless, JSON responses; outside `/api/v1`). Auth: `X-API-Key: opk_…`
or `Authorization: Bearer opk_…`. Tools and the scope each needs: `list_agents`, `describe_agent`
(`agents:read`), `run_agent` (`agents:run`), `start_workflow` (`workflows:write`),
`get_workflow_run` (`workflows:read`), `list_pending_approvals` (`approvals:read`),
`search_knowledge` (`documents:read`). Errors come back as MCP tool errors (`isError: true`) with
the platform's message. Host header must match `MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.

### Health & metrics
`GET /api/v1/health` (public: version, LLM mode, worker mode; used by the dashboard and `start.ps1`), `GET /health/live`, `GET /health/ready` (503 when DB unreachable or production config unsafe), `GET /metrics` (Prometheus).

## Tenant policy settings (`PATCH /admin/tenant` → `settings.policies`)

```json
{
  "approval_mode": "standard",            // or "strict": every side effect needs approval
  "amount_threshold": 1000,               // payload amounts above this need approval
  "external_comms_require_approval": true,
  "separation_of_duties": true,
  "approval_ttl_hours": 48,
  "denied_tools": ["commerce.create_purchase_order"],
  "auto_approve": [                       // narrow allowlists only; critical-risk tools can never be auto-approved
    {"name": "receipts", "tool": "email.send", "conditions": {"template_id_in": ["TPL-RECEIPT"]}},
    {"name": "ops-chat", "tool": "chat.post_message", "conditions": {"channel_in": ["#ops"]}}
  ]
}
```

articles.body:
Scope: the OpsPilot platform (API, workers, dashboard, database, integrations, LLM providers).
Method: STRIDE over the trust boundaries below, with mitigations that exist in code today and
residual risks called out explicitly.

## Assets

1. Tenant business data (leads, customers, orders, invoices, transcripts, documents).
2. Integration credentials and webhook secrets.
3. The ability to trigger external side effects (emails, WhatsApp, tickets, POs, payables).
4. Approval decisions and the audit trail (non-repudiation).
5. LLM spend / quotas.
6. User identities and roles.

## Trust boundaries

```
Internet ──► [B1] API edge (TLS, auth, rate limits)
API ──► [B2] Orchestrator/agents (untrusted content enters prompts here)
Agents ──► [B3] Policy engine + approvals (only path to side effects)
Platform ──► [B4] Providers (live adapters) and LLM providers
Platform ──► [B5] Database (tenant isolation) and object storage
Dashboard (browser) ──► [B6] API
```

## Threats and mitigations

| ID | Threat (STRIDE) | Mitigation in code | Residual / operator action |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | **Spoofing** a tenant via forged tenant id / claims | Tenant derived only from verified JWT (`tid` + user lookup must match) or API key row; forged tokens with unknown users rejected (test `test_tenant_claim_in_token_cannot_be_forged`) | Protect `SECRET_KEY`; prefer OIDC with RS256 + JWKS |
| T2 | **Spoofed webhooks** inject events | HMAC verification per provider (OpsPilot `t=,v1=` with 5-min replay window; Meta `sha256=`; Shopify base64), per-integration secrets, tenant resolved from path + verified | Rotate webhook secrets; monitor `webhook.signature_invalid` audit events |
| T3 | **Tampering** with an approved action between approval and execution | Approval bound to `sha256(tool, action_type, payload, tenant, agent)`; mismatch → `superseded` + critical audit event; reviewer may echo the hash they saw | DB write access is itself privileged; alert on `approval.tampered` |
| T4 | **Tampering** with the audit log | Each event stores a SHA-256 content hash; a single sealer per tenant links committed events into a gap-free chain (`seq`, `prev_hash`, `chain_hash`); `GET /audit-events/verify` recomputes every content hash and link, so edits and deletions are detected; on PostgreSQL the app role has no UPDATE/DELETE except the three chain columns, and a trigger refuses to change a sealed event or any event's content (tests: `tests/integration/test_audit_chain.py`, run on SQLite and PostgreSQL) | Events are unsealed for ≤ 1 min after writing; the oldest retained event is the trust anchor after retention; anyone with the DB owner role can rewrite history, so ship sealed chain heads (or the events) to an external WORM store |
| T5 | **Repudiation** of approvals | Reviewer id, timestamp, note and execution result stored; decisions only by human principals (API keys refused); separation of duties | Enforce MFA at the IdP |
| T6 | **Information disclosure** across tenants | `tenant_id` on every table + application filters; PostgreSQL RLS policies; sandbox records tenant-scoped; cross-tenant tests | Run DB as `opspilot_app` so RLS is active; never query with the owner role |
| T7 | **Information disclosure** of secrets | Credentials Fernet-encrypted; API keys stored as SHA-256; log/serializer redaction of secret-looking keys and bearer tokens; credentials write-only in API; error handler never returns stack traces | Store `ENCRYPTION_KEY` in a secrets manager; rotation runbook |
| T8 | **Prompt injection** via customer messages, transcripts, documents, reviews | Untrusted text wrapped as data with explicit instruction; pattern scan → warnings and escalation to humans; agents validate outputs deterministically (citations must match retrieved sources, numbers must exist in inputs, owners must resolve in the directory); the model never decides policy; tools are allowlisted per agent | New injection styles evade regexes: keep humans in the loop for high-risk actions (default policy) |
| T9 | **Elevation of privilege** by the model ("grant yourself admin") | Permissions come from roles/API-key scopes only; policy engine evaluates tool allowlists + actor permissions; critical tools always need approval; `platform:admin` is never implied by `*` | — |
| T10 | **Elevation of privilege** by users | Role grants limited to the granter's own permissions; cannot remove own admin/deactivate self; quotas/plans only for `platform:admin` | — |
| T11 | **Malicious documents** (active PDF content, embedded instructions, secrets) | Type/size allow-list, scan for `/JavaScript`, `/Launch`, `/OpenAction`, injection patterns and credential patterns; flagged docs excluded from retrieval | Add AV scanning (ClamAV) at upload in regulated environments |
| T12 | **Denial of service** / cost abuse | Per-tenant rate limits (Redis or in-memory), monthly workflow/token quotas, per-agent token budgets, tool-call caps, workflow step limits and deadlines, bounded delegation depth, request size limits | Edge WAF / IP throttling |
| T13 | **Duplicate / runaway side effects** (replays, retries, crashes) | Event dedupe keys, `Idempotency-Key`, derived idempotency keys on actions, `in_progress` marker before provider calls, verification instead of blind retry for non-idempotent tools, dead-letter queue, circuit breakers | Live adapters without native idempotency (Slack, SendGrid) rely on verification; review `tool_executions.status = unknown` |
| T14 | **Unsafe automation** (sending, paying, deploying) | Agents only propose; external comms, payables, POs, listing publication, rollbacks require approval; agents literally lack tools to pay or deploy; emergency disable per tenant | Keep `auto_approve` rules narrow; review them in audits |
| T15 | **Supply chain** | Pinned dependencies, `pip-audit`, `bandit`, Trivy image scan in CI, non-root container | Enable Dependabot/Renovate; sign images |
| T16 | **Data retention / privacy** | Tenant `retention_days`; retention job; protected characteristics stripped before scoring; consent checks before outreach | Define lawful basis per channel; DSAR tooling |
| T17 | **SSRF via custom tools** (tenant admin, or a model-chosen input, points a tool at `169.254.169.254`, `localhost`, an internal service, or a host that redirects / DNS-rebinds there) | https only; host resolved before the call and **every** resolved address must be globally routable (loopback, RFC 1918, link-local, CGNAT, multicast, reserved, IPv6 ULA/link-local and IPv4-mapped all refused); redirects disabled; input values are URL-encoded into the template and cannot change scheme/host; response size and timeout capped; tests parametrised over private/metadata addresses | A TOCTOU window remains between the resolution check and the connection (DNS rebinding with TTL 0). In production also route egress through a proxy that enforces the same rule, and keep `CUSTOM_TOOLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK=false` |
| T18 | **Custom tool secrets** leaking | Auth header value Fernet-encrypted, write-only in the API (`has_secret` only), never put in prompts, tool results or audit details | Prefer narrowly-scoped tokens for the target API |
| T19 | **Model-driven tool misuse** in the Copilot (prompt injection in tool results steering the model to call a side-effecting tool) | The model only sees tools the caller's RBAC allows; built-in tools exposed to it are read-only; agents it calls still propose and the policy engine still decides; side-effecting custom tools always require approval bound to the payload hash; iteration and tool-call caps; every call is a persisted, audited step | Approvers must read the exact payload shown, not the Copilot's summary of it |
| T20 | **MCP endpoint abuse** (unauthenticated use, over-scoped keys, DNS rebinding from a browser) | Every tool call authenticates a tenant API key and checks the scope the tool needs; same policy/approval/audit path as the REST API; API keys cannot decide approvals; Host header allow-list (`MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`); stateless transport (no session to hijack) | Issue MCP keys with the minimum scopes and an expiry; rotate on staff changes |
| T21 | **Queue poisoning / starvation** (one tenant floods jobs; a poison job crashes workers repeatedly) | Per-tenant concurrency cap on claims, job dedupe keys, bounded attempts with backoff then `dead`, leases so a crashed worker's job is retried elsewhere, workflow run lease so a retried job cannot double-execute a run | Alert on dead jobs and queue depth (`/system/queue`) |

## Abuse cases exercised by tests

`tests/security/test_security.py` covers: cross-tenant reads/writes, forged tokens, unlisted and
side-effecting tool calls from agents, tool-call limits, prompt injection in messages and
transcripts, malicious PDF upload, webhook signature/replay/handshake, secret leakage in API
and audit, privilege escalation, model self-authorisation, security headers and correlation-id
sanitisation. `tests/integration/test_approvals_and_actions.py` covers approval tampering,
expiry, separation of duties, exactly-once execution, reconciliation and duplicate suppression.
`tests/integration/test_copilot_tools_batches_mcp.py` covers SSRF refusals (loopback, RFC 1918,
link-local metadata, CGNAT, IPv6 loopback and ULA, IPv4-mapped IPv6), invalid tool definitions, side-effecting custom tools
requiring approval and executing once, Copilot session privacy and permissions, and MCP calls with
missing, invalid and under-scoped API keys. `tests/integration/test_scale_queue.py` covers
exactly-once job claims under concurrency, tenant caps, lease expiry and the run lease.

## Out of scope / assumptions

* The IdP, network, and cloud account are configured securely.
* LLM providers are trusted with tenant data under contract; use a provider with zero-retention
  terms or self-hosted models for regulated data. The mock provider sends nothing externally.
* Live provider adapters have not been security-reviewed against each vendor's current API
  behaviour in this repository.

articles.body:
**A multi-tenant AI workforce platform: 25 specialist business agents on one shared, policy-gated, auditable orchestration engine.**

OpsPilot receives business events, picks the right workflow and specialist agent, executes
authorised actions through typed tools, pauses for human approval on anything consequential,
recovers from failures without duplicating side effects, and records everything.

| | |
|---|---|
| Backend | Python 3.12 · FastAPI · Pydantic v2 · SQLAlchemy 2 · Alembic · PostgreSQL (SQLite for local dev) · Celery/Redis (thread pool for local dev) |
| AI | Provider-agnostic LLM gateway (Anthropic, OpenAI, deterministic mock) · structured outputs · token budgets · cost tracking · optional pgvector RAG |
| Frontend | Next.js 14 · React 18 · TypeScript · Tailwind · TanStack Query · Recharts · React Flow |
| Ops | Docker + Compose · GitHub Actions CI · OpenTelemetry + Prometheus · hash-chained audit log |

> **Honesty note.** Out of the box every integration runs in **sandbox mode** against synthetic
> tenant data, and the LLM provider is a **deterministic mock** (each agent ships a heuristic
> implementation of its model calls). Everything is end-to-end functional without credentials;
> nothing is ever reported as "connected" or "sent" unless a real provider was configured,
> its connection test passed, and the call succeeded. See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](/help/architecture#what-is-mock-vs-live).

## Quick start (local, no Docker)

Prerequisites: Python 3.10+ (3.12 recommended), Node.js 20+.

**Windows: double-click `start.cmd`** (or run it from a terminal). It:

- finds a real Python (skipping the Microsoft Store stub) and Node;
- creates the venv, installs pinned dependencies (only when requirements change) and writes `.env` with freshly generated `SECRET_KEY` / `ENCRYPTION_KEY`;
- frees ports held by a previous OpsPilot run (or picks the next free port), seeds the demo tenant;
- starts the API, waits for `/api/v1/health`, builds and starts the dashboard, and opens http://localhost:3000.

```powershell
start.cmd                                   # API :8000 + dashboard :3000 (production build)
scripts\start.ps1 -Dev                      # hot-reload dashboard (next dev)
scripts\start.ps1 -Workers 4                # + 4 separate worker processes (WORKER_MODE=db)
scripts\start.ps1 -ApiPort 8100 -WebPort 3100 -NoBrowser
stop.cmd                                    # stop everything it started
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\doctor.ps1   # "it doesn't work": diagnoses ports, venv, .env, API, proxy
```

Logs are in `.run/logs/`. The dashboard calls the API through its own same-origin proxy
(`/api/v1/*` → `OPSPILOT_API_ORIGIN`), so there are no CORS or `localhost` vs `127.0.0.1`
mismatches; the login page shows a red banner with the fix if the API is not reachable.

```bash
# macOS / Linux
cp .env.example .env
cd backend && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m app.cli seed            # creates SQLite schema, syncs the agent catalog, seeds the demo tenant
python -m app.cli serve           # API on http://127.0.0.1:8000  (OpenAPI docs at /docs)
# optional, for real horizontal scale: WORKER_MODE=db python -m app.workers.runner --concurrency 4
# in a second terminal
cd frontend && cp .env.local.example .env.local && npm install && npm run dev   # http://localhost:3000
```

Demo accounts (tenant slug `acme-demo`, password `OpsPilot-Demo-2026!`, **local development only**):

| Email | Role | Can |
|---|---|---|
| admin@acme-demo.test | admin | everything in the tenant (not plans/quotas) |
| ops@acme-demo.test | operator | run agents/workflows, manage tasks |
| approver@acme-demo.test | approver | decide approvals incl. external sends |
| finance@acme-demo.test | finance_approver | approve payables / purchase orders |
| auditor@acme-demo.test | auditor | read audit trail and reports |
| viewer@acme-demo.test | viewer | read-only dashboards |

## Quick start (Docker Compose: PostgreSQL + Redis + Celery)

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # set SECRET_KEY and ENCRYPTION_KEY
docker compose up --build       # api :8000, web :3000, worker, beat, db, redis
```

The `migrate` service runs `alembic upgrade head` and seeds the demo tenant before the API starts.

## Deploy (Render / Vercel)

API on Render via the `render.yaml` Blueprint (Render → New → Blueprint), database on
Neon, dashboard on Render or Vercel (root directory `frontend`, env `OPSPILOT_API_ORIGIN` = API URL).
Always set `DEMO_PASSWORD` on a public deployment. Step by step:
[docs/DEPLOYMENT.md → Render / Vercel](/help/deployment#render--vercel-hosted-demo).

## Try the demo in 60 seconds

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/login -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"tenant":"acme-demo","email":"ops@acme-demo.test","password":"OpsPilot-Demo-2026!"}' | jq -r .access_token)

# 1. A new lead arrives → qualified → CRM record → outreach drafted → waits for approval
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/events -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"source":"webform","event_type":"lead.created","external_id":"demo-1","payload":{"lead":{"name":"Ana Silva","email":"ana@globex.test","company":"Globex","title":"VP Operations","industry":"logistics","company_size":900,"budget":80000,"timeline":"this quarter","message":"We need to automate warehouse exception handling."}}}'

# 2. See the run, its checkpoints, agent outputs and the pending approval
curl -s localhost:8000/api/v1/workflows?limit=1 -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq '.items[0] | {id,status,current_node}'
curl -s "localhost:8000/api/v1/approvals?status=pending" -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq '.items[0] | {id,tool_key,risk_level,reason,payload_hash}'
```

Approve it from the dashboard (Approval Center) as `approver@acme-demo.test`, or via
`POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/decision`. The run resumes and completes; the "email" lands in the
sandbox outbox (never sent anywhere).

Other end-to-end demos (also run by the CLI and the test-suite):

```bash
cd backend
python -m app.cli run-workflow meeting_to_tasks  --input '{"meeting_id":"MTG-1"}'
python -m app.cli run-workflow customer_query    --input '{"message":"How long does standard shipping take?","customer_id":"C-2001"}'
python -m app.cli run-workflow invoice_to_review --input "{\"document_text\":\"$(cat docs/samples/invoice_ok.txt)\"}"
python -m app.cli run-workflow release_watch     --input '{"service":"checkout-api","deployment_id":"DEP-301"}'
python -m app.cli run-workflow kpi_report        --input '{"period_days":14,"months":3}'
python -m app.cli evaluate                        # runs all 25 synthetic evaluation datasets
```

## Ops Copilot: agents and tools driven by the model

The **Copilot** page (`/copilot`, API `POST /api/v1/copilot/sessions`) is a chat front-end over
the whole platform. Each turn runs a bounded tool-use loop in which the model can call:

| Tool family | What it does | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| `agent__<key>` (25) | runs a specialist agent; its proposed actions go through the policy engine as usual | approvals created → step shows `needs_approval` |
| `<family>__<op>` (27) | read-only registry tools: orders, shipments, inventory, KPIs, tasks, SOPs, invoices… | read-only by allow-list |
| `ops__*` | list agents / approvals / workflows, get a run, start a workflow | caller's RBAC |
| `custom__<name>` | your tenant's own HTTP tools (below) | side-effecting ones always require approval |

Several tool calls in one model turn run together and their results go back in one message;
failures return as `is_error` results the model can recover from; iterations and tool calls are
capped (`COPILOT_MAX_ITERATIONS`, `COPILOT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS`). Every step is persisted and shown live.
With `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` the loop is driven by Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`, adaptive effort,
prompt caching, server-side fallbacks). With the mock provider a deterministic offline planner
drives the same loop, so the page works without a key. Each answer records which mode produced it.

Turns run on the job queue, never in the request: `POST .../messages` returns immediately and
the UI polls the session.

## Custom tools (bring your own API)

Admins register HTTPS endpoints as tools (Integrations → Custom tools, or `POST /api/v1/custom-tools`):
name, method, URL template, JSON input schema, optional secret header (Fernet-encrypted at rest),
and `side_effect`. The tool is then usable by the Copilot as `custom__<name>`.

Guard-rails: https only; DNS is resolved and **every** address must be public (no loopback,
RFC 1918, link-local/metadata, CGNAT…); no redirects; per-tool timeout (default 15 s); 256 KB
response cap; input validated against the schema; side-effecting calls need an approval bound
to the exact payload hash and run exactly once with an idempotency key.
`POST /custom-tools/{id}/test` makes one real call with sample input and shows you the actual
response; nothing is pre-filled or simulated.

## MCP server (use OpsPilot from Claude Desktop, Claude Code, any MCP client)

The API serves a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp` with tools
`list_agents`, `describe_agent`, `run_agent`, `start_workflow`, `get_workflow_run`,
`list_pending_approvals`, `search_knowledge`. Authenticate with a tenant API key
(`POST /api/v1/admin/api-keys`, e.g. scopes `["agents:read","agents:run","workflows:read","workflows:write","approvals:read","documents:read"]`):

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http opspilot http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp --header "X-API-Key: opk_..."
```

Scopes are enforced per tool, and everything an MCP client does goes through the same policy
engine, approvals and audit log as the dashboard. For a public host add it to `MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.

## Scaling

| `WORKER_MODE` | Who executes workflows, Copilot turns, bulk items | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `inline` | the calling thread | tests |
| `thread` (default) | a worker pool inside the API process, fed by the durable DB queue | single machine |
| `db` | any number of `python -m app.workers.runner --concurrency N` processes / containers on the same DB | horizontal scale |
| `celery` | Celery workers via Redis (workflows) | existing Celery estates |

The queue lives in the `jobs` table: on PostgreSQL workers claim with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.
Each claim takes a lease that the worker renews; a crashed worker's leases expire and the jobs
return to the queue with backoff, and go to `dead` after `max_attempts` (retry from `/system`).
Jobs are deduplicated (`dedupe_key`), tenants have a concurrency cap (`max_concurrent_runs`) so one
tenant cannot starve the others, and a workflow run additionally holds an atomic run lease so two
workers can never execute the same run. **Bulk runs** (`POST /api/v1/agents/{key}/batches`, up to
5,000 items) fan out one job per item; a stuck item whose worker died is reclaimed.
`/system` in the dashboard shows the queue, live workers and dead jobs.

Measured with real worker processes on one laptop (mock LLM): on PostgreSQL a 300-item bulk run
went from 14 to 21 items/s with 1 → 4 worker processes. Hard-killing a worker mid-run lost no items
and duplicated no side effects. SQLite gets no benefit from more workers. Full table and caveats
in [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md → Scale benchmark](/help/deployment#scale-benchmark).

## Repository layout

```
backend/
  app/
    agents/           base contract, registry, runner, services; catalog/ = the 25 agents (one module each)
    orchestration/    workflow engine (graph runner, checkpoints, resume, parallel, delegation), built-in definitions
    policy/           deterministic policy engine (allow / require_approval / deny)
    services/         actions (execute + reconcile), approvals, audit, usage, retrieval, maintenance, documents
    tools/            typed tool registry + catalog (98 tools) + platform adapter
    integrations/     adapter contract, 13 sandbox adapters, 7 live adapters, resolver, resilience helpers
    llm/              provider-agnostic gateway, mock provider, prompt-injection safety
    api/              FastAPI routes (v1), schemas, serializers, auth deps
    db/               SQLAlchemy models (28 tables), portable types, session
    workers/          thread/Celery queue, scheduler, maintenance jobs
    evaluation/       synthetic datasets + harness
    seed/             roles/permissions, catalog sync, demo tenant data
  alembic/            migrations (initial schema + PostgreSQL RLS/append-only hardening)
  tests/              unit · integration · security · agents · e2e  (236 tests; run on SQLite and PostgreSQL)
  load/               scale benchmark: real API + worker processes, crash test, exactly-once checks
frontend/             Next.js dashboard (see frontend/README.md)
docs/                 ARCHITECTURE · API · DEPLOYMENT · THREAT_MODEL · KPI_AND_ROI · EVALUATION_REPORT_TEMPLATE
docker-compose.yml · .github/workflows/ci.yml · .env.example · scripts/dev.ps1 · Makefile
```

## The 25 agents

| 3 | Sales | Sales Call Intelligence (`sales_call_intelligence`) | consent flag required |
| 4 | Sales | Proposal Generator (`proposal_generator`) | approval before delivery; deal desk for non-standard terms |
| 5 | Support | Customer Support (`customer_support`) | escalates unsupported/sensitive queries |

| 7 | Support | WhatsApp Business (`whatsapp_business`) | opt-in, 24h window, templates, approval |

Each agent declares its contract (input/output schemas, allowed tools, permission scopes,
policies, approval rules, budgets) in code; `GET /api/v1/agents/{key}` exposes it.

## Testing

```bash
cd backend
pytest -q                         # 236 tests: unit, integration, security, per-agent, e2e (SQLite)
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://…/empty_db pytest -q   # the same suite on PostgreSQL (schema via Alembic)
python -m load.scale_benchmark --check                         # multi-process throughput + crash test
python -m app.cli evaluate        # synthetic evaluation datasets (precision/recall, accuracy, intervention rate…)
ruff check app tests
```

Tests use SQLite, the mock LLM provider and sandbox adapters: no network, no real customer
data, no real messages. CI additionally runs the migrations and a smoke evaluation against
PostgreSQL, `pip-audit`, `bandit`, builds both containers and scans them with Trivy.

## Configuration

See [`.env.example`](/help/configuration). Key switches:

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | `sqlite:///./opspilot.db` (dev) or `postgresql+psycopg://…` (prod) |
| `WORKER_MODE` | `inline` (tests) · `thread` (dev) · `db` (separate `app.workers.runner` processes) · `celery` (needs `REDIS_URL`) |
| `WORKER_CONCURRENCY`, `JOB_LEASE_SECONDS` | in-process pool size; how long before a dead worker's jobs are re-queued |
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `mock` · `anthropic` (+`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) · `openai` (+`OPENAI_API_KEY`) |
| `LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `LLM_EFFORT`, `COPILOT_EFFORT` | model (`claude-opus-5-5`) and effort per tier |
| `COPILOT_MAX_ITERATIONS`, `COPILOT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS` | hard bounds on one Copilot turn |
| `MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | Host headers the `/mcp` endpoint accepts (DNS-rebinding protection) |
| `CUSTOM_TOOLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK` | `false` by default; only for an isolated on-prem network you control |
| `SECRET_KEY`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY` | JWT signing and Fernet encryption of integration credentials |
| `OIDC_ISSUER`, `OIDC_JWKS_URL`, `OIDC_AUDIENCE` | SSO; set `ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN=false` once configured |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| Dashboard opens but nothing loads / login fails | run `scripts\doctor.ps1`; the login page banner says whether the API is reachable through the proxy |
| `start.cmd` says a port is busy | it frees ports held by an old OpsPilot run itself; otherwise it picks the next free port and prints it |
| `python` opens the Microsoft Store | the WindowsApps stub; install Python from python.org, `start.cmd` skips the stub |
| Copilot message stays "thinking" | no worker is running: `WORKER_MODE=db` needs at least one `app.workers.runner`; check `/system` |
| Jobs in `dead` on `/system` | they failed `max_attempts` times; read `last_error`, fix, press Retry |
| `email-validator is not installed` | `pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt` (pinned) |
| Login returns 422 for `*.test` addresses | fixed: the API uses a syntactic e-mail check (RFC deliverability is the IdP's job) |
| `/health/ready` returns 503 | DB unreachable, or in production: unsafe `SECRET_KEY`, SQLite, missing `ENCRYPTION_KEY` |
| Runs stay `pending` | `WORKER_MODE=celery`/`db` without a worker; start `celery -A app.workers.celery_app:celery_app worker -Q workflows` / `python -m app.workers.runner`, or use `thread` |
| Run stuck `running` after a crash | the maintenance job (every 60 s) re-enqueues stale runs; `python -m app.cli maintenance` runs it once |
| Agent returns `agent_disabled` (423) | agent disabled for the tenant or tenant emergency-disabled (Admin → Tenant) |
| Integration shows `error` | the live connection test failed; see `last_error`; it stays unusable (sandbox fallback) until a test passes |
| Approvals return 409 | expired, already decided, or payload hash mismatch (re-request approval) |
| Windows: `winget` installed Python/Node but commands not found | open a new terminal, or use the full paths in `scripts/dev.ps1` |

articles.summary: Every setting OpsPilot reads, generated from the configuration templates in the repository so it always matches the code.
articles.body:
Every setting OpsPilot reads, generated from the configuration templates in the repository so it always matches the code.

## Where settings live

- **API and workers:** a `.env` file in the project root (a copy of `.env.example`). `start.cmd` creates one with fresh random secrets on first run. Real environment variables override the file.
- **Dashboard:** `frontend/.env.local` (a copy of `frontend/.env.local.example`).
- **Hosted deployments (Render, Vercel, Docker):** set the same names as environment variables in the platform's settings.
- **Secrets:** API keys, database passwords, `SECRET_KEY` and `ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Never commit `.env` files or paste these into tickets or chat.

## Minimum for production

`/health/ready` reports what is missing. You need: `APP_ENV=production`, a PostgreSQL `DATABASE_URL`, a strong `SECRET_KEY`, an `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, an LLM provider with its API key, single sign-on (`OIDC_*`) with `ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN=false`, `DEMO_PASSWORD` if the demo tenant is seeded, and your public host in `CORS_ORIGINS` and `MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. See the [deployment guide](/help/deployment).

## Common setups

| Goal | Set |
|---|---|
| Neon (serverless PostgreSQL) | `DATABASE_URL` = the Neon connection string from the **direct** endpoint (host without `-pooler`), `ENABLE_PGVECTOR=true`, `DB_POOL_SIZE=5` |
| Gemini | `LLM_PROVIDER=gemini`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, Gemini model ids in `LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL` / `LLM_FAST_MODEL`, `LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8192` |
| Claude | `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, Claude model ids |
| Fully offline | `LLM_PROVIDER=mock` and the SQLite `DATABASE_URL` (the defaults) |
| More background workers | `WORKER_MODE=db`, then extra `python -m app.workers.runner` processes (or `start.cmd -Workers N`) |

## API and workers (`.env`)

### Application

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `APP_ENV` | `development` | development \| test \| staging \| production |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` |  |
| `LOG_JSON` | `false` |  |
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:3000,http://127.0.0.1:3000` |  |

### Database

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | `sqlite:///./opspilot.db` | Local dev default is SQLite (zero setup). Production MUST use PostgreSQL. Neon (serverless PostgreSQL): paste the connection string from Neon Console -> Connect. Use the DIRECT endpoint (host without "-pooler"): this app keeps its own connection pool, sets per-session lock timeouts and runs DDL migrations. postgres:// / postgresql:// are accepted as-is. Examples: `postgresql+psycopg://opspilot:opspilot@localhost:5432/opspilot`, `postgresql://<user>:<password>@ep-<name>-<id>.<region>.aws.neon.tech/<db>?sslmode=require&channel_binding=require`. |
| `ENABLE_PGVECTOR` | `false` | Neon ships pgvector; enables vector search for document chunks Examples: `true`. |
| `DB_POOL_SIZE` | *(not set)* | per process (API + each worker); keep the total under your compute's max_connections Examples: `5`. |
| `DB_POOL_RECYCLE_SECONDS` | *(not set)* | Neon suspends idle compute (default 5 min) and drops connections Examples: `300`. |

### Workers

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `WORKER_MODE` | `thread` | inline \| thread \| db \| celery   (db: run python -m app.workers.runner; celery requires REDIS_URL) |
| `REDIS_URL` | *(not set)* | Examples: `redis://localhost:6379/0`. |
| `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` | `4` | in-process pool size (thread mode) |
| `WORKFLOW_MAX_STEPS` | `50` |  |
| `WORKFLOW_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `600` |  |
| `JOB_LEASE_SECONDS` | `120` | a crashed worker's jobs return to the queue after this |
| `BATCH_ITEM_STALE_SECONDS` | `300` | a bulk-run item stuck "running" this long is reclaimed |

### Security

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `SECRET_KEY` | `change-me-to-a-long-random-value` | Generate: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))" |
| `ENCRYPTION_KEY` | *(empty)* | Generate: python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())" |
| `ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN` | `true` | set false once OIDC is configured |
| `OIDC_ISSUER` | *(not set)* | Examples: `https://login.example.com/`. |
| `OIDC_AUDIENCE` | *(not set)* | Examples: `opspilot-api`. |
| `OIDC_JWKS_URL` | *(not set)* | Examples: `https://login.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json`. |
| `WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET` | *(empty)* | fallback secret for X-OpsPilot-Signature webhooks (per-integration secrets preferred) |
| `DEMO_PASSWORD` | *(not set)* | Password for the seeded demo accounts. Leave unset locally (public default, shown on the login page); ALWAYS set it on an internet-facing deployment. Re-running the seed rotates existing demo accounts. |
| `ALLOW_SIGNUP` | `true` | self-serve "Create a workspace" for new companies |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `600` |  |
| `APPROVAL_DEFAULT_TTL_HOURS` | `48` |  |

### LLM

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `auto` | auto (first key found: gemini, anthropic, openai) \| mock \| anthropic \| openai \| gemini |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | *(not set)* | Add one or more keys. With several, OpsPilot fails over between them automatically when one is rate-limited, out of quota or down; with none, agents use their built-in logic. Google AI Studio key (free tier: ~20 requests/day per model) |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | *(not set)* |  |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | *(not set)* |  |
| `LLM_FALLBACK_PROVIDERS` | *(not set)* | auto = every other keyed provider \| none \| e.g. anthropic,openai Examples: `auto`. |
| `GEMINI_FALLBACK_MODELS` | *(not set)* | each has its own free quota Examples: `gemini-3.8-flash,gemini-3.5-flash-lite`. |
| `GEMINI_MODEL` | *(not set)* | per-provider defaults Examples: `gemini-3.6-flash  ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5  OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4o`. |
| `LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL` | `claude-opus-5-5` | LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL / LLM_FAST_MODEL override the primary provider's models, e.g. with Gemini: LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash  LLM_FAST_MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash  LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8192 (Gemini counts thinking tokens toward the output limit; effort maps to thinking_level) |
| `LLM_FAST_MODEL` | `claude-opus-5-5` | fast tier = same model at lower effort |
| `LLM_EFFORT` | `medium` | low \| medium \| high \| xhigh \| max |
| `LLM_FAST_EFFORT` | `low` |  |
| `LLM_ENABLE_FALLBACKS` | `true` | server-side model fallback on overload |
| `LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `60` |  |
| `LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | `2048` |  |

### Ops Copilot / tools / MCP

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `COPILOT_EFFORT` | `high` |  |
| `COPILOT_MAX_ITERATIONS` | `8` |  |
| `COPILOT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS` | `24` |  |
| `CUSTOM_TOOLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK` | `false` | keep false: blocks SSRF to internal/metadata addresses |
| `MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | `127.0.0.1:*,localhost:*,testserver` | add your public API host in production |

### Observability

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OTEL_ENABLED` | `false` |  |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | *(not set)* | Examples: `http://otel-collector:4318/v1/traces`. |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | `opspilot-api` |  |
| `METRICS_ENABLED` | `true` |  |

### Documents

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND` | `local` | local \| s3 |
| `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_PATH` | `./storage` |  |
| `S3_BUCKET` | *(not set)* |  |
| `S3_REGION` | *(not set)* |  |
| `MAX_DOCUMENT_SIZE_MB` | `25` |  |

### Frontend

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OPSPILOT_API_ORIGIN` | `http://127.0.0.1:8000` | The dashboard proxies /api/v1/* to this origin (server side), so the browser never needs CORS. |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` | *(not set)* | only to bypass the proxy and call the API directly Examples: `https://api.example.com/api/v1`. |

## Dashboard (`frontend/.env.local`)

### Settings

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OPSPILOT_API_ORIGIN` | `http://127.0.0.1:8000` | The dashboard proxies /api/v1/* to the OpsPilot API at runtime (app/api/v1/[...path]/route.ts). Where the API lives (read when the dashboard server starts; no rebuild needed): |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` | *(not set)* | Optional: bypass the proxy and call an API on another origin directly from the browser. Leave unset for the default same-origin setup (recommended). Examples: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1`. |
